pr_narrative: This change hardens SWE-AF along three fronts proven during the FCM-only L3 acceptance campaign. First, it completes provider enablement: OpenCode gains [OI]-compatible Gonka and FCM providers, the package contract accepts OPENAI_API_KEY, and SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL defaults to the virtual fcm/fcm id so FCM owns upstream routing. Second, it converts the textual no-install rule that models overran (l3-21 pip installs) into runtime enforcement: one shared OpenCodeNoInstallPermissionOverlay, fed identically to coder, reviewer and verifier, denies dependency installation and cross-worktree virtualenv execution while keeping normal read/test/build commands allowed — verified live by canaries on the real OpenCode/FCM path. Third, it repairs weak-model structured-output handling: harnessx Run delegates to a single executeStructured policy seam with per-role SchemaMode override, CoderResult tolerates agent_retro-as-string, and run_qa_synthesizer now validates via isinstance(QASynthesisResult) with an explicit fail-safe fallback plus a production-path regression test. HITL gains an opt-in OpenClaw/Telegram fallback and richer decision_context at every ask_user call site. PLAN.md records the L3-19/20/21 checkpoints, the closed gates (FCM argv, coder no-install, reviewer fail-closed grading, live enforcement), and the remaining open gate (repair -> verifier -> delivery on a delivered SHA).
risk_surfaces: Permission overlay semantics: the bash rule set mixes a catch-all "*" allow with specific deny patterns; correct behaviour depends on OpenCode's precedence for deny-over-allow and longest-prefix matching — a runtime regression there silently reopens the install escape route.
Role wiring drift: coder, reviewer and verifier must all receive the same overlay string; prompt/testdata and role code duplicate it textually, and golden tests are the only drift guard.

CoderResult.UnmarshalJSON leniency: accepting agent_retro as a plain string weakens the strict schema contract for one field; if weak models emit other mistyped fields, they still hard-fail — callers relying on previously-fatal behaviour should be re-checked.

OpenClaw HITL is process-local (atomic counter ids, Agent.Pause) and opt-in, but enabling it changes approval routing to Telegram/webhook paths whose reachability and authentication are deployment-specific.
AGENTFIELD_HARNESS_IDLE_SECONDS=0 disables the idle-output watchdog; liveness then depends solely on the SDK total timeout, so a hung harness subprocess will hold a slot until hard timeout.
SchemaMode per-role override can silently change structured-output reliability per role; no metric gates which roles may use single-shot mode.

Large mixed delta (58 files, Go + Python + prompts + testdata) makes exact-SHA canonicalization sensitive: acceptance evidence in PLAN.md was gathered on an earlier subset of this live delta, so revalidation of the exact delivered identity is still required.
